universe: NSE Nifty Total Market + top-250 by turnover

ladder.note: Targets sit on a level price turned at where one exists in range, otherwise on the R floor, which is labelled. `reach` is the measured share of closed trades that ran at least that far — cf_1h and intraday are excluded from that sample because their max-favourable figures are not credible.

ahimsa.note: Membership in NSE's index, not a score. NSE publishes no per-company quotient and this build computes none. It is not an input to any score on this page.

rules.roc: ROCE — EBIT ÷ invested capital, latest fiscal year (the screen's own figure)
rules.ey: EBIT ÷ enterprise value; EV = market cap + total debt − cash
rules.combine: rank each separately (1 = best), add the two ranks, lowest sum first; ties go to the higher earnings yield
rules.exclude: lenders, insurers and real estate (the screen's lender rule), utilities, market cap under ₹1,000 cr, no statements, statements older than 18 months, a one-off year, EBIT or EV not positive
rules.source: Joel Greenblatt, The Little Book That Still Beats the Market (2010)
rules.deviation: Return on capital uses ROCE on invested capital, not Greenblatt's net working capital + net fixed assets; EBIT is the last fiscal year, not the trailing twelve months; a year whose EBIT margin moved 15+ points is unranked as a likely one-off; EV carries no minority-interest line, so a holding company that consolidates a listed subsidiary can read cheaper than it is.

magic_formula.note: A ranking of current figures, not a prediction. The book reports a sustained edge in the US over 1988–2009; it has also had multi-year stretches of trailing the market. Nothing here says what any of these companies will do.

lenses.label: Momentum
lenses.rule: Above its 50 and 200-day averages, ahead of the Nifty over three months, RSI 55 to 75

tests.label: Sales growth
tests.note: The rule asks for 10 years. The screen holds four fiscal years of statements, so this is the 3-year compound rate.

tests.label: Return on capital
tests.note: The rule asks for a 10-year average. This is the median of the fiscal years held, at most four.

tests.label: Insider holding
tests.note: The rule asks for promoter holding, which this screen does not have. This is Yahoo's insiders figure, a wider bucket than SEBI's promoters, so read it as a proxy.

tests.label: Share return
tests.note: The rule asks for 10 years. The screen holds four years of prices, so this is 3 years, and a recent listing has none.

tests.label: Debt to equity
tests.note: Negative equity is insolvency, so it does not pass. Not defined for lenders.

tests.label: Net profit
tests.note: The rule reads Net profit over 10%. It is read here as net profit margin.

tests.label: Operating cash flow
tests.rule: positive in each of the last 3 fiscal years

rules.label: Statements
rules.rule: Three or more fiscal years of annual statements

rules.label: Fresh statements
rules.rule: Latest fiscal year ended within 18 months

rules.label: Fresh price
rules.rule: Last close within 5 days of the screen's price date

rules.label: Market cap
rules.rule: Market cap published and at least ₹1,000 cr

rules.label: Leverage
rules.rule: Debt to equity at least 0 and under 2 (not applicable to lenders)

rules.label: Interest cover
rules.rule: EBIT covers interest at least 3 times (not applicable to lenders)

rules.label: Cash conversion
rules.rule: Median operating cash flow at least 80% of profit (not applicable to lenders)

rules.label: Run rate
rules.rule: Latest EBIT margin did not move 15+ points in a year (not applicable to lenders)

vet.note: Cleared means a company passed these checks on the data held, and held means the stated reason. It is not a score, a ranking or a recommendation, it feeds no other number on this page, and nothing here predicts a company or its price.
